title: Sonata Brevis
identity: Bertold Hummel's *Sonata brevis*, Op. 95a (1991), is an 18-minute, three-movement work for E-flat alto saxophone and piano, written at saxophonist Normand DesChênes's suggestion and dedicated to him. Hummel's site describes a two-theme sonata opening, a hymn quotation in the arch-shaped slow movement, and a variable-metre rondo finale that ends in a virtuoso stretta. It lists the 1993 premiere and professional recordings.

evidence.claim: Composer foundation provides instrumentation, date, duration, movements, dedication, premiere, formal/technical descriptions, autograph references, and publisher number.
Composer discography identifies Lutz Koppetsch and Markus Bellheim 2007 recording.
The publisher-hosted one-page sample PDF shows the opening alto saxophone part, titled Sonata Brevis, Op.95a, I. Allegro, with quarter note = 144 and measures 1-31 visible.
evidence.source_name: Alfred Music / Advance Music sample score

score_observations.observation: Inspected the publisher-hosted one-page preview of the E-flat alto saxophone part, covering the opening 31 measures of I. Allegro. It begins at quarter note = 144. The visible part uses frequent accidentals, slurs and accent markings, pronounced shifts in dynamics from p/pp to sf/f/ff, and later beamed/triplet figures that make the notation denser than the opening bars. This preview is one part page and does not show the piano writing or complete saxophone range.

review_focus: Inference from the inspected excerpt and the composer’s movement descriptions: review accurate chromatic reading and controlled dynamic extremes in the opening, then compare the later triplet/denser figures with the publisher-described variable metre and virtuoso Presto. The preview only covers the Allegro opening.
collection_flag: Original work written for and premiered by a professional saxophonist; no youth transcription concern.

listening.description: Composer discography identifies a 2007 recording by Lutz Koppetsch and Markus Bellheim
